cases.source: pub struct Alpha; pub struct Beta; impl Alpha { pub fn used(&self)->u32 {1} pub fn limit(&self)->u32 {2} } impl Beta { pub fn size(&self)->u32 {let read=||3; read()} pub fn capacity(&self)->u32 {4} } pub fn alpha(x:&Alpha)->(u32,u32) {(x.used(),x.limit())} pub fn beta(y:&Beta)->(u32,u32) {(y.size(),y.capacity())}

pub struct Alpha { pub value:u32 } pub struct Beta { pub value:u32 } impl Alpha { pub fn measure(&self)->u32 { self.value+1 } } impl Beta { pub fn amount(&self)->u32 { let read=||self.value; read()+2 } } pub enum Item { A(Alpha), B(Beta) } pub fn dispatch(item:&Item)->u32 { match item { Item::A(a)=>a.measure(), Item::B(b)=>b.amount() } }

invariants: Fresh original checked findings are required before any user dismissal; stored choices never supply declaration or pairing authority.
Lookup never creates, rewrites, migrates or prunes the store.
Line positions and formal names are presentation; selected context, declaration/member identities and ordered roles are relevant.
Opaque callee bodies are excluded from durable identity because the proposal requires declaration signatures rather than body admission.
Helper schema1 remains readable and unchanged until explicit source-family addition creates schema2; helper and source-family decisions remain independent.
Hidden known findings do not erase unavailable owners or exhausted scope.
Invalid selectors, malformed stores and duplicate dismissals must not write.
